title: F8-bis RESEARCH: capital structure as commitment device (UK, US, NL, Singapore)
description: Operator extension of the F8 ruling: doc 16 covered judicial-review DESIGN; this covers a different mechanism family, capital structure as a commitment device that makes cancellation expensive. Source hypothesis supplied by the operator from an external model, to be TESTED not assumed: UK Sizewell C (state enters the cap table, so cancelling destroys the state's own equity), US (SPV plus TIFIA plus private activity bonds, many parties with simultaneous exposure), Netherlands (DBFM, performance-conditioned long-term contract), Singapore (state as developer/landlord/shareholder via JTC and GLCs), France (the contrast: strong administration but veto points stay open after sunk costs). Four strands verify each model against primary sources and report where the supplied hypothesis is wrong. Deliverable: docs/precedent-research/19-capital-commitment-devices.md with sections per model, a verification ledger of the supplied claims (CONFIRMED/CORRECTED/UNVERIFIED), and mechanism hooks. The load-bearing hook to develop: the sequencing lesson - contest first, commit after - mapped onto the appellate verb so a record's challenge window narrows as dependents accumulate.
acceptance_criteria: docs/precedent-research/19-capital-commitment-devices.md exists with one section per model (UK, US, NL, Singapore, France as contrast), a verification ledger of the operator-supplied claims, and mechanism hooks
every operator-supplied claim is explicitly marked CONFIRMED, CORRECTED (with the correct fact) or UNVERIFIED - an externally-supplied hypothesis is never restated as fact without a source
at least 10 distinct external sources cited inline, primary where available (government statements, statutes, agency pages); no emojis; no absolute user paths

mechanism hooks include the sequencing property (contest window closes as dependents accumulate) tied to the researched instrument it derives from, and state honestly which hooks the harness CANNOT use because it has no capital
verifier (non-producer) replayed doc against strand findings and spot-checked at least 3 citations before verdict

DEFECT 1 (blocking). Sec 4, the I-77 termination price, is not supported by the primary source and is contradicted by it, while being carried as [ESTABLISHED] and elevated to load-bearing status in three places.
The doc asserts: "NCDOT commissioned an analysis that priced state termination after completion at $400M to more than $600M" (sec 4), repeats it in sec 2.5 ("NCDOT obtained a $400M-to-$600M+ figure for exiting I-77 and declined"), and builds K8's watch-for shape on it in sec 8.3. Sec 4 calls it "the cleanest demonstration in the whole four-model record that capital structure changes a decision."
I retrieved the actual commissioned analysis from NCDOT's own site: Mercator Advisors LLC, "Review of the Comprehensive Agreement for the I-77 Express Lanes Project", FINAL REPORT, September 2017 (ncdot.gov, /projects/i-77-express-lanes/Documents/mercator-final-report.pdf). It contains no $400M-$600M figure anywhere. Its Table 9, the only termination pricing in the report, gives illustrative Termination Compensation as of 31 December 2016 of $149M (Scenario A), $149M (Scenario B) and $168M (Scenario C), against a separately noted State Auditor expert estimate of about $300M fair market value as of 31 October 2015. The only "$600 million" in the report is an unrelated USDOT grant pool at page reference line 199. The report states plainly that its scenarios "are not indications of the potential cost to terminate the CA for convenience in the future", so it does not price post-completion termination at all. My searches surfaced no dated press item carrying $400M-$600M either; WFAE's contemporaneous reporting is that the Transportation Secretary said NCDOT could not buy out the contract.
This is exactly the failure the document exists to prevent: a confident number arriving through secondary press attribution (the US strand's own source line reads "Mercator Advisors analysis reported by WFAE and Carolina Public Press"), promoted to [ESTABLISHED], and then made the single cleanest demonstration in the argument. Under doc 13's own load-bearing test it is load-bearing, and it does not hold.
REQUIRED FIX: replace the figure with the primary one, or demote the claim. The good news is that the primary source strengthens sec 2.5 and K8 rather than weakening them. Mercator states directly, at the head of the illustrative example: "The payments due upon a termination for convenience are not intended to be a penalty that discourages the public agency from exercising its termination rights. The complicated provisions for calculating the amounts due under different circumstances are designed to protect the interests of both NCDOT and the Private Partner." That is a first-party statement by the analyst the state hired that termination compensation is not a deterrent, which is the doc's own K8 thesis stated by the instrument itself. Rewrite sec 4 to cite Mercator September 2017 Table 9 and that sentence; adjust sec 2.5's one-line restatement; and either drop "priced state termination after completion at $400M to more than $600M" or mark it UNVERIFIED with the primary contradiction recorded, since an unsourceable number in this document must be treated the way UK-15 and SG-5 were treated.

DEFECT 2 (minor, fix in passing). Sec 5 states of the Dutch formula: "Most components are floored at zero, so netting cannot claw the payout below invested capital." The contract text I extracted says the opposite about the total: "De bedragen V en KFO kunnen negatief zijn" - V itself may be negative; it is HS, AL, Aand, RV1, RV2, AltR, Verz, Bel and the sum (RV2-AltR) that are floored at zero. The first clause is right, the inference in the second clause overreaches. Strand-inherited, but it should say that the individual components are floored while V itself is not.
